```{r}

library(ggplot2)

pos <- read.csv("polar_pos_pqn_imputed_glog.csv", row.names=1)
# rows are features, so transpose for PCA
mat <- t(pos[, -1])  # drop the mz column

pca <- prcomp(mat, scale.=TRUE)
scores <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2])
scores$site <- sub("[AB][0-9]$", "", rownames(scores))

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, color=site)) + geom_point(size=3) +
  labs(title="Positive mode metabolomics PCA")

```

```{r}

pos_mat <- read.csv("polar_pos_pqn_imputed_glog.csv", row.names=1)
mz_col <- pos_mat$mz
pos_mat <- pos_mat[, -1]  # remove mz

site <- sub("[AB][0-9]$", "", colnames(pos_mat))

pvals <- apply(pos_mat, 1, function(x) {
  summary(aov(x ~ site))[[1]]["site", "Pr(>F)"]
})

adj_pvals <- p.adjust(pvals, method="BH")
sig_features <- names(adj_pvals[adj_pvals < 0.05])
cat("Significant features:", length(sig_features), "\n")


```

```{r}


# =============================================================================
# COMPLETE METABOLOMICS EDA PIPELINE — NEGATIVE ION MODE
# Purpose: Confirm data quality BEFORE sending to MetaboAnalyst
# Author: Snehal Senthil
# Data: polar_neg_pqn_imputed_glog.csv (already PQN + KNN + glog processed)
# =============================================================================
# WHY DO EDA BEFORE METABOANALYST?
# MetaboAnalyst is a black box — it won't warn you if a sample is broken,
# if your group labels are wrong, or if your data structure is misread.
# EDA in R gives you full control and transparency over every decision.
# If something is wrong and you catch it here, your downstream statistics
# are trustworthy. If you skip EDA and send bad data, all results are invalid.
# =============================================================================

# ── STEP 0: INSTALL AND LOAD PACKAGES ────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY: Each package serves a specific purpose described inline.
cat("Installing/loading packages...\n")
needed <- c("ggplot2", "pheatmap", "reshape2", "matrixStats",
            "dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "ggrepel",
            "RColorBrewer", "viridis", "patchwork", "scales")

for (pkg in needed) {
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)      # all plotting
  library(pheatmap)     # heatmaps with annotations
  library(reshape2)     # data reshaping (melt)
  library(matrixStats)  # fast row/col variance, median
  library(dplyr)        # data manipulation
  library(tidyr)        # pivot/separate
  library(tibble)       # rownames_to_column
  library(ggrepel)      # non-overlapping text labels on plots
  library(RColorBrewer) # colour palettes
  library(viridis)      # perceptually uniform colour scales
  library(patchwork)    # combine ggplots
  library(scales)       # axis formatting
})
cat("✓ Packages loaded\n\n")

# ── STEP 1: SET YOUR WORKING DIRECTORY ───────────────────────────────────────
# Change this to wherever your data files are stored
# BASE_DIR <- "~/DataJamboree"                    # Mac/Linux
BASE_DIR <- "~/Computational_Biology/CompBio_Files"   # current directory — change this!
setwd(BASE_DIR)


# ── STEP 2: LOAD THE DATA ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY THIS FILE: polar_neg_pqn_imputed_glog.csv is the fully preprocessed
# negative ion mode data. The name tells you its history:
#   pqn        = probabilistic quotient normalisation (corrects for dilution)
#   imputed    = KNN imputation applied (missing values filled)
#   glog       = generalised log transformation (stabilises variance)
# This is the analysis-ready file. You do NOT use the raw or pqn-only files.
cat("Loading data...\n")
raw <- read.csv(
  file.path(BASE_DIR, "polar_neg_pqn_imputed_glog.csv"),
  row.names = 1,         # first col = feature IDs (e.g. "75_02526269")
  check.names = FALSE    # IMPORTANT: stops R mangling sample names like D01A1
)
# The second column is "mz" — the m/z value used for annotation.
# It is a FEATURE DESCRIPTOR, not a sample. We separate it now.
mz_values <- raw$mz                    # save m/z for annotation later
feat_mat   <- raw[, colnames(raw) != "mz"]  # pure intensity matrix

cat("✓ Data loaded\n")
cat("  Features (peaks):   ", nrow(feat_mat), "\n")
cat("  Samples:            ", ncol(feat_mat), "\n")
cat("  First 5 feature IDs:", paste(rownames(feat_mat)[1:5], collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("  First 5 sample IDs: ", paste(colnames(feat_mat)[1:5], collapse=", "), "\n\n")

# ── STEP 3: LOAD SAMPLE SHEET ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY: The sample sheet tells us which sample belongs to which site and
# concentration. Without it we can't colour plots or run grouped statistics.
ss <- read.csv(file.path(BASE_DIR, "sample_sheet.csv"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(ss) <- c("sample_id", "concentration", "site", "description")
ss$concentration <- factor(ss$concentration,
                            levels = c("Control", "1x", "10x"))
ss$site <- factor(ss$site,
                  levels = c("Control", paste0("D", sprintf("%02d", 1:12))))
cat("✓ Sample sheet loaded:", nrow(ss), "rows\n\n")

# ── STEP 4: PARSE METADATA FROM SAMPLE NAMES ─────────────────────────────────
# WHY: The metabolomics file sample names encode site, batch (A/B), and
# replicate number. We decode these for use in plots and statistics.
# Naming convention: D06B3 = Site D06, Batch B (=10x), Replicate 3
#                   D01A2 = Site D01, Batch A (=1x), Replicate 2
#                   CK07  = Control replicate 7

decode_sample <- function(ids) {
  data.frame(
    sample_id   = ids,
    site        = ifelse(grepl("^CK", ids), "Control",
                         regmatches(ids, regexpr("D[0-9]{2}", ids))),
    batch       = ifelse(grepl("^CK", ids), "Control",
                         sub(".*(A|B)[0-9]$", "\\1", ids)),
    replicate = as.integer(regmatches(ids, regexpr("\\d+$", ids))),
    concentration = ifelse(grepl("^CK", ids), "Control",
                    ifelse(grepl("A[0-9]$", ids), "1x", "10x")),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

meta <- decode_sample(colnames(feat_mat))
meta$site         <- factor(meta$site,
                             levels = c("Control",
                                        paste0("D", sprintf("%02d", 1:12))))
meta$concentration <- factor(meta$concentration,
                              levels = c("Control", "1x", "10x"))
rownames(meta) <- meta$sample_id

cat("✓ Metadata parsed from sample names\n")
cat("  Sites found:        ", paste(levels(meta$site), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("  Concentrations:     ", paste(levels(meta$concentration), collapse=", "), "\n\n")

# ── STEP 5: BASIC DIMENSION AND COMPLETENESS CHECKS ──────────────────────────
# WHY: We need to confirm:
# (a) expected number of samples are present
# (b) sample IDs in the data match the sample sheet
# (c) there are truly no missing values (since KNN imputation was applied)
# (d) the data is numeric throughout

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 5: DIMENSION AND COMPLETENESS CHECKS\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

# 5a: Expected vs actual sample counts
# Negative mode is known to have 145 samples (positive has 149)
cat("\n5a — Sample counts per group:\n")
site_counts <- table(meta$site)
print(site_counts)
# EXPECTED: Control=6, D01=11 (one failed QC), D02-D12=12 each
# If D01 shows 11 that is correct and documented — not a data error

View(meta)
cat("\nConcentration counts:\n")
print(table(meta$concentration))
# EXPECTED: Control=6, 1x=~72, 10x=~72 (minus the D01 missing sample)

# 5b: Check which sample sheet samples are NOT in the metabolomics data
cat("\n5b — Sample sheet samples missing from metabolomics data:\n")
missing_from_met <- setdiff(ss$sample_id, colnames(feat_mat))
if (length(missing_from_met) == 0) {
  cat("  None — perfect match\n")
} else {
  cat("  Missing:", paste(missing_from_met, collapse=", "), "\n")
  cat("  Count:", length(missing_from_met), "\n")
  # WHY THIS MATTERS: These samples were lost during LC-MS acquisition
  # (injection failure, instrument issue). This is normal in real studies.
  # We simply work with what we have.
}

# 5c: Extra samples in metabolomics NOT in sample sheet
extra_in_met <- setdiff(colnames(feat_mat), ss$sample_id)
cat("\n5c — Metabolomics samples NOT in sample sheet:\n")
if (length(extra_in_met) == 0) {
  cat("  None\n")
} else {
  cat("  Extra:", paste(extra_in_met, collapse=", "), "\n")
}

# 5d: Missing values
n_na <- sum(is.na(feat_mat))
n_total <- prod(dim(feat_mat))
cat("\n5d — Missing values:\n")
cat("  Total NA cells:    ", n_na, "\n")
cat("  Total cells:       ", n_total, "\n")
cat("  % missing:         ", round(100 * n_na / n_total, 4), "%\n")
if (n_na == 0) {
  cat("  ✓ CONFIRMED: No missing values — KNN imputation was successful\n")
  cat("  EVIDENCE: The file suffix '_imputed' and 0% missing values\n")
  cat("  together confirm imputation was applied before you received the data.\n")
} else {
  cat("  !! WARNING: Missing values remain — investigate before MetaboAnalyst\n")
}

# 5e: Confirm all data is numeric
non_numeric <- sum(!sapply(feat_mat, is.numeric))
cat("\n5e — Data type check:\n")
cat("  Non-numeric columns:", non_numeric, "\n")
if (non_numeric == 0) cat("  ✓ All columns numeric\n")

# 5f: Value range check (glog values should be roughly 7-15)
cat("\n5f — Value range (expect glog ≈ 7–15 for metabolomics):\n")
cat("  Global min:  ", round(min(feat_mat, na.rm=TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  Global max:  ", round(max(feat_mat, na.rm=TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  Global mean: ", round(mean(unlist(feat_mat), na.rm=TRUE), 3), "\n")
# WHY: glog-transformed metabolomics data should sit in this range.
# Values outside 5-20 suggest the wrong file was loaded or transformation failed.

cat("\n")

# ── STEP 6: SAMPLE-LEVEL QC ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY: Even after PQN normalisation, a catastrophically broken sample
# (e.g. injection failure, sample swap, contamination) will have a
# mean intensity far from all others. We detect these visually and
# statistically using ±2 SD flagging.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 6: SAMPLE-LEVEL QC\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

# Calculate per-sample statistics
sample_stats <- data.frame(
  sample_id  = colnames(feat_mat),
  mean_int   = colMeans(feat_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
  median_int = apply(feat_mat, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_int     = apply(feat_mat, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  cv_int     = apply(feat_mat, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) /
               colMeans(feat_mat, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
)
sample_stats <- merge(sample_stats, meta, by = "sample_id")

# Flag outliers: mean intensity > 2 SD from overall mean
global_mean <- mean(sample_stats$mean_int)
global_sd   <- sd(sample_stats$mean_int)
sample_stats$outlier_flag <- abs(sample_stats$mean_int - global_mean) >
                             3 * global_sd
sample_stats$outlier_label <- ifelse(sample_stats$outlier_flag,
                                     sample_stats$sample_id, "")

cat("Global mean intensity:", round(global_mean, 3), "\n")
cat("Global SD:            ", round(global_sd, 3), "\n")
cat("Flagged samples (>3SD):", sum(sample_stats$outlier_flag), "\n")
if (any(sample_stats$outlier_flag)) {
  cat("  Flagged:", paste(sample_stats$sample_id[sample_stats$outlier_flag],
                          collapse=", "), "\n")
}

# PLOT 6a: Mean intensity per sample with 2SD flagging bands
p6a <- ggplot(sample_stats %>% arrange(site, concentration),
              aes(x = reorder(sample_id, as.numeric(site)),
                  y = mean_int,
                  colour = site,
                  shape  = concentration)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = global_mean, colour = "black",
             linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = global_mean + 2 * global_sd,
             colour = "#D62728", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = global_mean - 2 * global_sd,
             colour = "#D62728", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = outlier_label),
                  size = 2.5, colour = "#D62728", max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Control"=16, "1x"=17, "10x"=15)) +
  labs(title    = "Sample QC: Mean glog intensity per sample",
       subtitle = "Red dashed = ±2SD boundary; labelled points = potential outliers",
       x = "Sample (ordered by site)",
       y = "Mean glog intensity",
       colour = "Site", shape = "Concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
# INTERPRETATION: Points outside the dashed lines are outlier candidates.
# After PQN, we expect most samples to cluster tightly. A few outliers
# are acceptable in environmental studies due to biological variability.
# Only remove a sample if it is BOTH a statistical outlier AND there is
# a documented technical reason (e.g. injection failure log entry).

print(p6a)
ggsave("qc_01_mean_intensity_per_sample.pdf", p6a, width = 14, height = 5)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_01_mean_intensity_per_sample.pdf\n")

# PLOT 6b: Boxplot distributions per sample
# WHY: After PQN normalisation, all sample boxes should align at roughly
# the same median and have similar spread. A sample whose box is shifted
# far up or down failed normalisation or has a systematic problem.
# We show a random subset of 40 samples to keep it readable.
set.seed(42)
show_samps <- sample(colnames(feat_mat),
                     min(40, ncol(feat_mat)), replace = FALSE)
box_df <- feat_mat[, show_samps, drop = FALSE] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("feature_id") %>%
  pivot_longer(-feature_id, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "glog_int") %>%
  left_join(meta[, c("sample_id","site","concentration")], by = "sample_id")

# Order samples by site for visual grouping
box_df$sample_id <- factor(box_df$sample_id,
                            levels = show_samps[order(
                              meta[show_samps, "site"],
                              meta[show_samps, "concentration"])])

p6b <- ggplot(box_df, aes(x = sample_id, y = glog_int, fill = site)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3,
               linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(title    = "Sample QC: Distribution of glog intensities (random 40 samples)",
       subtitle = "After PQN, all boxes should align at similar median (~8-9)",
       x = NULL, y = "glog intensity") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 6),
        legend.position = "bottom")
# INTERPRETATION GUIDE:
# - All boxes at similar height = PQN worked correctly ✓
# - One box shifted high or low = that sample may be problematic
# - Similar box widths = similar variance across samples ✓
# - Outlier dots above whiskers = high-intensity peaks (normal in metabolomics)

print(p6b)
ggsave("qc_02_sample_boxplots.pdf", p6b, width = 14, height = 6)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_02_sample_boxplots.pdf\n\n")

# PLOT 6c: Overall density plot
# WHY: The global intensity distribution should be unimodal and roughly
# symmetric after glog transformation. A bimodal distribution would suggest
# two distinct data populations (batch effect or file mixing).
all_vals <- unlist(feat_mat)
dens_df  <- data.frame(glog_int = all_vals[!is.na(all_vals)])

p6c <- ggplot(dens_df, aes(x = glog_int)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#4575B4", alpha = 0.6, colour = "#2166AC") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(dens_df$glog_int),
             colour = "#D62728", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title    = "Global intensity density distribution",
       subtitle = "Should be unimodal; dashed = mean; glog data peaks ~7-9",
       x = "glog intensity", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
# EVIDENCE FOR PQN + GLOG SUCCESS:
# - Unimodal peak = no major batch effects splitting the data
# - Peak around 7-9 = consistent with properly glog-transformed LC-MS data
# - Long right tail = a few high-abundance metabolites (biologically expected)

print(p6c)
ggsave("qc_03_global_density.pdf", p6c, width = 7, height = 5)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_03_global_density.pdf\n\n")

# ── STEP 7: FEATURE-LEVEL QC ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY: Just as samples can be broken, features (peaks) can be uninformative.
# Peaks with near-zero variance across all samples carry no information
# for distinguishing groups. We identify them here.
# NOTE: We are NOT removing them yet — that happens in MetaboAnalyst
# using the IQR filter we discussed. Here we just characterise them.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 7: FEATURE-LEVEL QC\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

feat_stats <- data.frame(
  feature_id  = rownames(feat_mat),
  mz          = mz_values,
  mean_int    = rowMeans(feat_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_int      = rowSds(as.matrix(feat_mat), na.rm = TRUE),
  median_int  = rowMedians(as.matrix(feat_mat), na.rm = TRUE),
  iqr_int     = apply(feat_mat, 1, IQR, na.rm = TRUE),
  cv_pct      = rowSds(as.matrix(feat_mat), na.rm = TRUE) /
                rowMeans(feat_mat, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
)

# Near-zero variance features
nzv_threshold <- 0.01  # IQR < 0.01 = essentially constant
n_nzv <- sum(feat_stats$iqr_int < nzv_threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Features with IQR < 0.01 (near-zero variance):", n_nzv, "\n")
cat("Proportion:", round(100 * n_nzv / nrow(feat_stats), 2), "%\n")
# EXPECTED: Very few near-zero variance features because KNN imputation
# tends to preserve local variance structure.

# PLOT 7a: Variance (IQR) distribution across all features
p7a <- ggplot(feat_stats, aes(x = iqr_int)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 80, fill = "#2CA02C", colour = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = nzv_threshold, colour = "#D62728",
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, quantile(feat_stats$iqr_int, 0.99))) +
  labs(title    = "Feature variance distribution (IQR across all samples)",
       subtitle = paste0("Red line = near-zero variance threshold (", nzv_threshold,
                         "); features left of line = uninformative"),
       x = "IQR of glog intensity", y = "Number of features") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
# INTERPRETATION:
# - Most features should have IQR > 0.1 (some variation between samples)
# - Features at IQR ≈ 0 are flat lines — no discriminating power
# - The distribution shape tells you how variable your metabolome is overall

print(p7a)
ggsave("qc_04_feature_variance.pdf", p7a, width = 8, height = 5)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_04_feature_variance.pdf\n")

# PLOT 7b: Mean-Variance relationship
# WHY: This is the key plot to confirm glog transformation worked.
# In raw LC-MS data, high-abundance features also tend to have high variance
# (mean-variance dependency). Glog transformation should BREAK this dependency,
# making variance relatively flat across the mean range.
p7b <- ggplot(feat_stats, aes(x = mean_int, y = sd_int)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8, colour = "#4575B4") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = "#D62728",
              linewidth = 1.2, se = TRUE) +
  labs(title    = "Mean-Variance relationship across features",
       subtitle = "After glog: variance should be FLAT (no trend) — confirms transformation success",
       x = "Mean glog intensity (feature average across samples)",
       y = "SD of glog intensity") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
# EVIDENCE FOR GLOG SUCCESS:
# - If the loess line is flat = glog removed mean-variance dependency ✓
# - If the loess line slopes upward = transformation insufficient (unlikely
#   since glog is specifically designed to fix this in LC-MS data)
# - This plot is your primary evidence that glog transformation was effective

print(p7b)
ggsave("qc_05_mean_variance.pdf", p7b, width = 8, height = 5)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_05_mean_variance.pdf\n\n")

# PLOT 7c: CV% distribution
# WHY: Coefficient of variation (SD/mean * 100) tells you what % of the
# mean intensity is "noise". In untargeted metabolomics, CV < 30% per feature
# is generally acceptable. High CV features are noisy.
p7c <- ggplot(feat_stats, aes(x = cv_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#FF7F0E", colour = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 30, colour = "#D62728",
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(title    = "Feature CV% distribution",
       subtitle = "Red line = 30% threshold; features right of line are high-noise",
       x = "CV% (SD/Mean × 100)", y = "Number of features") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
n_high_cv <- sum(feat_stats$cv_pct > 30, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Features with CV > 30%:", n_high_cv, "(", 
    round(100*n_high_cv/nrow(feat_stats),1), "%)\n")

print(p7c)
ggsave("qc_06_cv_distribution.pdf", p7c, width = 8, height = 5)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_06_cv_distribution.pdf\n\n")

# ── STEP 8: PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS ─────────────────────────────────────
# WHY PCA IN EDA: PCA reduces 2331 features to a few axes of maximum variance.
# It lets you see the overall structure of the data in 2D:
# - Are samples from the same site close together? (within-group reproducibility)
# - Are there obvious outlier samples far from their group? (QC failures)
# - Does the data separate by site, concentration, or neither?
# We use the TOP 1000 most variable features for PCA speed and signal clarity.
# Using all 2331 features would dilute the signal with uninformative peaks.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 8: PCA — STRUCTURE AND OUTLIER DETECTION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

feat_var  <- rowVars(as.matrix(feat_mat))
top1000   <- order(feat_var, decreasing = TRUE)[1:1000]
pca_input <- t(feat_mat[top1000, ])   # samples as rows

# scale.=TRUE: z-score each feature before PCA so high-intensity peaks
# don't dominate just because they are abundant
pca_res <- prcomp(pca_input, scale. = TRUE)
pct_var  <- round(100 * pca_res$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2), 1)

pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:5])
pca_df$sample_id    <- rownames(pca_df)
pca_df <- merge(pca_df, meta, by = "sample_id")
pca_df$concentration <- factor(pca_df$concentration,
                                levels = c("Control","1x","10x"))

cat("Variance explained:\n")
for (i in 1:5) cat("  PC", i, ":", pct_var[i], "%\n")
cat("  Cumulative PC1-5:", sum(pct_var[1:5]), "%\n\n")

# Colour palettes (same as main EDA script)
SITE_COLS <- c(
  "Control"="#000000","D01"="#E6194B","D02"="#3CB44B",
  "D03"="#4363D8","D04"="#F58231","D05"="#911EB4",
  "D06"="#42D4F4","D07"="#F032E6","D08"="#BFEF45",
  "D09"="#FABED4","D10"="#469990","D11"="#DCBEFF","D12"="#9A6324"
)
CONC_COLS <- c("Control"="#2CA02C","1x"="#1F77B4","10x"="#D62728")
UPSTREAM_COLS <- c(
  "Control"="#888888",
  setNames(colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC","#74ADD1","#ABD9E9",
                               "#FFFFBF","#FDAE61","#F46D43",
                               "#D73027"))(12),
           paste0("D",sprintf("%02d",1:12)))
)

# PLOT 8a: PC1 vs PC2 coloured by site (unique colours)
p8a <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2,
                           colour = site,
                           shape  = concentration)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = SITE_COLS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Control"=16,"1x"=17,"10x"=15)) +
  labs(title    = "Metabolomics PCA — negative ion mode (PC1 vs PC2)",
       subtitle = "Unique colour per site; shape = concentration",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "%)"),
       colour = "Site", shape = "Concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p8a)

# PLOT 8b: PC1 vs PC2 upstream→downstream gradient
p8b <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2,
                           colour = site,
                           shape  = concentration)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = UPSTREAM_COLS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Control"=16,"1x"=17,"10x"=15)) +
  labs(title    = "Metabolomics PCA — upstream (blue) → downstream (red)",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "%)"),
       colour = "Site", shape = "Concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(p8b)

# PLOT 8c: Coloured by concentration
p8c <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = concentration)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = CONC_COLS) +
  labs(title    = "Metabolomics PCA — coloured by concentration",
       subtitle = "Tests whether dose (1x vs 10x) drives metabolome variance",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "%)"),
       colour = "Concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(p8c)

# PLOT 8d: PC2 vs PC3 (sometimes site effect appears in later PCs)
p8d <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC2, PC3, colour = site, shape = concentration)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = SITE_COLS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Control"=16,"1x"=17,"10x"=15)) +
  labs(title = "PC2 vs PC3 — negative ion mode",
       x = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC3 (", pct_var[3], "%)")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(p8d)

ggsave("qc_07_pca_4panel.pdf",
       (p8a | p8b) / (p8c | p8d),
       width = 14, height = 10)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_07_pca_4panel.pdf\n")

# INTERPRETATION GUIDE FOR PCA:
# - Tight clusters per site = good within-group reproducibility
# - Overlapping clusters across all sites = metabolome doesn't clearly
#   separate by site (signal is there but subtle — expected in env. studies)
# - Control samples (black circles) should NOT cluster with polluted sites
# - Any single sample far outside its group = QC failure candidate
# - If 10x squares consistently separate from 1x triangles along any PC
#   = concentration effect exists in the metabolome

# ── STEP 9: MAHALANOBIS DISTANCE OUTLIER DETECTION ───────────────────────────
# WHY: Visual PCA inspection is subjective. Mahalanobis distance is an
# objective, multivariate measure of how far each sample is from the
# centre of the PCA cloud, accounting for correlations between PCs.
# Samples with very high Mahalanobis distance are statistical outliers.
# We use the first 5 PCs (enough to capture main structure).
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 9: MAHALANOBIS DISTANCE OUTLIER DETECTION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

pc_scores <- pca_res$x[, 1:5]
tryCatch({
  mah_dist  <- mahalanobis(pc_scores,
                            center = colMeans(pc_scores),
                            cov    = cov(pc_scores))
  # Under multivariate normality, Mahalanobis distance² follows chi-squared
  # distribution with df = number of dimensions (5 PCs here)
  mah_pval  <- pchisq(mah_dist, df = 5, lower.tail = FALSE)
  mah_padj  <- p.adjust(mah_pval, method = "BH")
  
  mah_df <- data.frame(
    sample_id  = rownames(pc_scores),
    mah_dist   = mah_dist,
    mah_pval   = mah_pval,
    mah_padj   = mah_padj,
    outlier    = mah_padj < 0.05
  )
  mah_df <- merge(mah_df, meta, by = "sample_id")
  mah_df <- mah_df[order(mah_df$mah_dist, decreasing = TRUE), ]
  
  cat("Mahalanobis outliers (FDR < 0.05):", sum(mah_df$outlier), "\n")
  if (any(mah_df$outlier)) {
    cat("Outlier samples:\n")
    print(mah_df[mah_df$outlier, c("sample_id","site","concentration",
                                    "mah_dist","mah_padj")])
  } else {
    cat("✓ No statistically significant outliers detected\n")
  }
  
  # PLOT 9: Mahalanobis distances
  p9 <- ggplot(mah_df %>% arrange(mah_dist),
               aes(x = reorder(sample_id, mah_dist),
                   y = mah_dist,
                   colour = outlier,
                   shape  = concentration)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_text_repel(data = mah_df[mah_df$outlier |
                                    mah_df$mah_dist > quantile(mah_df$mah_dist,
                                                                0.95), ],
                    aes(label = sample_id), size = 2.5,
                    max.overlaps = 20) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE"="grey60","TRUE"="#D62728"),
                        labels = c("OK","Outlier FDR<0.05")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Control"=16,"1x"=17,"10x"=15)) +
    labs(title    = "Mahalanobis distance per sample (multivariate outlier test)",
         subtitle = "Red = statistically significant outliers (chi-sq test, FDR<0.05)",
         x = "Sample", y = "Mahalanobis distance",
         colour = "Status", shape = "Concentration") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
  
p9
ggsave("qc_08_mahalanobis.pdf", p9, width = 12, height = 5)
  cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_08_mahalanobis.pdf\n\n")
  
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("Mahalanobis calculation failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  cat("This can happen if PCA scores are singular. Try reducing df to 3.\n")
})

# ── STEP 10: WITHIN-SITE REPRODUCIBILITY ─────────────────────────────────────
# WHY: Biological replicates within the same site should have similar
# metabolite profiles. High CV within a site means either noisy biology
# or one replicate failed. We calculate per-site CV across all features
# and flag sites with unusually high variability.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 10: WITHIN-SITE REPRODUCIBILITY\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

site_cv_list <- lapply(levels(meta$site), function(s) {
  samp_ids <- meta$sample_id[meta$site == s]
  samp_ids <- samp_ids[samp_ids %in% colnames(feat_mat)]
  if (length(samp_ids) < 2) return(NULL)
  sub_mat  <- feat_mat[, samp_ids, drop = FALSE]
  cv_vals  <- apply(sub_mat, 1,
                    function(x) sd(x, na.rm=TRUE) /
                                mean(x, na.rm=TRUE) * 100)
  data.frame(site = s,
             median_cv = median(cv_vals, na.rm=TRUE),
             mean_cv   = mean(cv_vals, na.rm=TRUE),
             n_samples = length(samp_ids))
})
site_cv_df <- do.call(rbind, site_cv_list)
site_cv_df$site <- factor(site_cv_df$site,
                           levels = c("Control",
                                      paste0("D",sprintf("%02d",1:12))))

cat("Within-site median CV% per site:\n")
print(site_cv_df[order(site_cv_df$median_cv, decreasing=TRUE), ])

p10 <- ggplot(site_cv_df, aes(x = site, y = median_cv, fill = site)) +
  geom_col(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(median_cv,1),"%")),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SITE_COLS, guide = "none") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(site_cv_df$median_cv),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D62728") +
  labs(title    = "Within-site reproducibility: median CV% across features",
       subtitle = "Red dashed = overall mean CV; higher CV = more variable replicates",
       x = "Site", y = "Median CV% across all features") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
# INTERPRETATION:
# - Low CV (< 20%) = replicates are consistent within site ✓
# - High CV for one site = one replicate may have failed for that site
# - D01 has 11 samples (one missing) — if its CV is much higher than
#   others, the missing sample might have been an extreme outlier that
#   was correctly removed by the lab before giving you the data

print(p10)
ggsave("qc_09_within_site_cv.pdf", p10, width = 10, height = 5)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_09_within_site_cv.pdf\n\n")

# ── STEP 11: ANNOTATION COVERAGE ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY: Before you run pathway enrichment, you need to know what fraction
# of your features actually HAVE KEGG/HMDB annotations. Unannotated features
# cannot contribute to pathway enrichment — knowing the coverage upfront
# sets realistic expectations for your enrichment results.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 11: ANNOTATION COVERAGE\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

tryCatch({
  kegg_annot <- read.delim(
    file.path(BASE_DIR, "polar_neg_pkl_to_kegg_annotations.tsv"),
    header = FALSE, sep = "\t",
    col.names = c("feature_id", "mz", "kegg_ids"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fill = TRUE, quote = ""
  )
  hmdb_annot <- read.delim(
    file.path(BASE_DIR, "polar_neg_pkl_to_hmdb_annotations.tsv"),
    header = FALSE, sep = "\t",
    col.names = c("feature_id", "mz", "hmdb_ids"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fill = TRUE, quote = ""
  )
  
  n_feat        <- nrow(feat_mat)
  n_kegg        <- sum(kegg_annot$kegg_ids != "" &
                       !is.na(kegg_annot$kegg_ids))
  n_hmdb        <- sum(hmdb_annot$hmdb_ids != "" &
                       !is.na(hmdb_annot$hmdb_ids))
  n_both        <- sum(kegg_annot$feature_id[kegg_annot$kegg_ids != ""] %in%
                       hmdb_annot$feature_id[hmdb_annot$hmdb_ids != ""])
  n_unannotated <- n_feat - length(union(
    kegg_annot$feature_id[kegg_annot$kegg_ids != "" & !is.na(kegg_annot$kegg_ids)],
    hmdb_annot$feature_id[hmdb_annot$hmdb_ids != "" & !is.na(hmdb_annot$hmdb_ids)]
  ))
  
  cat("Total features:            ", n_feat, "\n")
  cat("With KEGG IDs:             ", n_kegg,
      "(", round(100*n_kegg/n_feat,1), "%)\n")
  cat("With HMDB IDs:             ", n_hmdb,
      "(", round(100*n_hmdb/n_feat,1), "%)\n")
  cat("With BOTH annotations:     ", n_both, "\n")
  cat("Unannotated (neither):     ", n_unannotated,
      "(", round(100*n_unannotated/n_feat,1), "%) — NORMAL in untargeted metabolomics\n")
  
  # Pie chart of annotation coverage
  annot_pie <- data.frame(
    category = c("KEGG only", "HMDB only", "Both", "Unannotated"),
    count    = c(n_kegg - n_both, n_hmdb - n_both,
                 n_both, n_unannotated)
  )
  annot_pie$pct   <- round(100 * annot_pie$count / n_feat, 1)
  annot_pie$label <- paste0(annot_pie$category, "\n", annot_pie$pct, "%")
  
  p11 <- ggplot(annot_pie, aes(x="", y=count, fill=category)) +
    geom_col(width=1, colour="white") +
    coord_polar("y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values=c("KEGG only"="#4575B4","HMDB only"="#D62728",
                                "Both"="#2CA02C","Unannotated"="#CCCCCC")) +
    geom_text(aes(label=label),
              position=position_stack(vjust=0.5), size=3.5) +
    labs(title    = "Annotation coverage — negative ion mode",
         subtitle = "Unannotated features are kept in statistics but excluded from pathway analysis",
         fill = NULL) +
    theme_void(base_size=12) +
    theme(legend.position="none")
  
  print(p11)
  ggsave("qc_10_annotation_coverage.pdf", p11, width=6, height=6)
  cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_10_annotation_coverage.pdf\n\n")
  
}, error=function(e) {
  cat("Annotation files not found — skipping annotation coverage.\n")
  cat("Error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  cat("Make sure polar_neg_pkl_to_kegg_annotations.tsv is in BASE_DIR\n\n")
})

# ── STEP 12: CORRELATION BETWEEN SAMPLES (HEATMAP) ───────────────────────────
# WHY: A sample-sample Pearson correlation heatmap shows whether samples
# from the same site/group are more similar to each other than to other groups.
# Diagonal = 1 (each sample perfectly correlated with itself).
# Strong block structure along the diagonal = good grouping.
# An isolated column/row with very low correlation = outlier sample.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 12: SAMPLE-SAMPLE CORRELATION HEATMAP\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

# Order samples by site then concentration
ordered_samps <- meta %>%
  arrange(site, concentration) %>%
  pull(sample_id)
ordered_samps <- ordered_samps[ordered_samps %in% colnames(feat_mat)]

cor_mat <- cor(feat_mat[, ordered_samps], method = "pearson")

# Annotation for heatmap
ann_col_df <- meta[ordered_samps, c("site","concentration")]
rownames(ann_col_df) <- ordered_samps

site_levels   <- levels(meta$site)
site_cols_hm  <- SITE_COLS[site_levels]
names(site_cols_hm) <- site_levels

ann_colors_hm <- list(
  site          = site_cols_hm,
  concentration = CONC_COLS
)

pheatmap(
  cor_mat,
  main              = "Sample-sample Pearson correlation (glog intensities)",
  color             = colorRampPalette(c("#4575B4","white","#D73027"))(100),
  annotation_col    = ann_col_df,
  annotation_row    = ann_col_df,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors_hm,
  show_rownames     = FALSE,
  show_colnames     = FALSE,
  border_color      = NA,
  fontsize          = 8,
  filename          = "qc_11_sample_correlation_heatmap.pdf"
)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_11_sample_correlation_heatmap.pdf\n")
# INTERPRETATION:
# - Deep red blocks along diagonal grouped by site = site-specific metabolome ✓
# - All values near 0.9-1.0 = high overall correlation (expected after PQN)
# - One row/column that's pale/blue everywhere = that sample is unlike all others
#   → strong evidence to investigate/remove that sample

cat("\n")

# ── STEP 13: SITE-LEVEL METABOLITE PROFILES ──────────────────────────────────
# WHY: Before running ANOVA, we can visually inspect whether the top
# variable features show different patterns across sites. This gives us
# confidence that a site effect actually exists before we run statistics.
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 13: SITE-LEVEL PROFILES (TOP VARIABLE FEATURES)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

top20_var_feats <- names(sort(feat_var, decreasing=TRUE))[1:20]

site_profile_df <- feat_mat[top20_var_feats, ] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("feature_id") %>%
  pivot_longer(-feature_id, names_to="sample_id", values_to="glog_int") %>%
  left_join(meta[,c("sample_id","site","concentration")],
            by="sample_id")

p13 <- ggplot(site_profile_df,
              aes(x = site, y = glog_int, fill = concentration)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size=0.3, linewidth=0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=CONC_COLS) +
  facet_wrap(~feature_id, scales="free_y", ncol=5) +
  labs(title    = "Top 20 most variable features — site-level profiles",
       subtitle = "If boxes differ across sites, site effect exists in metabolome",
       x=NULL, y="glog intensity", fill="Concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=8) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, size=5),
        strip.text=element_text(size=6))

print(p13)
ggsave("qc_12_top20_site_profiles.pdf", p13, width=14, height=10)
cat("✓ Plot saved: qc_12_top20_site_profiles.pdf\n\n")

# ── STEP 14: FINAL SUMMARY AND DECISION ──────────────────────────────────────
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("STEP 14: FINAL EDA SUMMARY\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("DATA QUALITY CHECKLIST:\n")
cat("────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("✓ Features:       ", nrow(feat_mat), "\n")
cat("✓ Samples:        ", ncol(feat_mat), "\n")
cat("✓ Missing values: ", sum(is.na(feat_mat)), "(KNN imputed)\n")
cat("✓ Data type:      All numeric\n")
cat("✓ Value range:    ",
    round(min(feat_mat),2), "to", round(max(feat_mat),2),
    "(consistent with glog)\n")
cat("✓ D01 has 11 samples (1 lost to QC) — unbalanced ANOVA handles this\n")
cat("\n")
cat("NORMALISATION EVIDENCE:\n")
cat("────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("• Filename suffix '_pqn' = PQN applied (sample-level dilution correction)\n")
cat("• Filename suffix '_imputed' = KNN imputation applied\n")
cat("• Filename suffix '_glog' = generalised log transformation applied\n")
cat("• Global value range ~7-15 = consistent with glog output\n")
cat("• Sample boxplots at similar medians = PQN correction successful\n")
cat("• Mean-variance plot (see qc_05) = if flat, glog was effective\n")
cat("\n")
cat("DECISION ON WHETHER TO SEND TO METABOANALYST:\n")
cat("────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("→ If no statistical outliers (Step 9) and mean-variance flat (Step 7):\n")
cat("  SEND AS-IS. Select None for normalisation and transformation.\n")
cat("\n")
cat("→ If 1-2 statistical outliers found (Step 9):\n")
cat("  Investigate: do they come from a specific site/replicate?\n")
cat("  Only remove if there is a TECHNICAL reason (not just statistical).\n")
cat("  With only 6 replicates per group, losing one is costly.\n")
cat("\n")
cat("→ For MetaboAnalyst filtering (Low-variance filter):\n")
cat("  Use IQR at 25% — removes near-zero variance peaks only.\n")
cat("  Do NOT apply abundance filter (already handled by PQN).\n")
cat("  Do NOT normalise or transform again.\n")
cat("\n")
cat("OUTPUT FILES GENERATED:\n")
cat("────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
for (f in c("qc_01_mean_intensity_per_sample.pdf",
            "qc_02_sample_boxplots.pdf",
            "qc_03_global_density.pdf",
            "qc_04_feature_variance.pdf",
            "qc_05_mean_variance.pdf",
            "qc_06_cv_distribution.pdf",
            "qc_07_pca_4panel.pdf",
            "qc_08_mahalanobis.pdf",
            "qc_09_within_site_cv.pdf",
            "qc_10_annotation_coverage.pdf",
            "qc_11_sample_correlation_heatmap.pdf",
            "qc_12_top20_site_profiles.pdf")) {
  cat("  •", f, "\n")
}
cat("\n✓ EDA COMPLETE — review plots above before proceeding to MetaboAnalyst\n")



```
